title: Properness in terms of colours at each vertex
statement: Let $G$ be a finite graph and let $C$ be a $k$-edge colouring of $G$, that is, an assignment of one of the colours $1, 2, \ldots, k$ to each edge. Then $C$ is proper — no two distinct edges that share a common endpoint receive the same colour — if and only if $c(v) = d(v)$ for every vertex $v$, where $c(v)$ is the number of distinct colours represented at $v$ and $d(v)$ is the degree of $v$.
hypotheses_covered: k-edge colouring C assigning a colour in {1,...,k} to each edge
replaced:
(6.3): \texttt{C} is proper $\Longleftrightarrow$ equality holds in (6.3) at every
vertex.

Moreover, $\mathscr{C}$ is a proper $k$-edge colouring if and only if equality
holds in (6.3) for all vertices $v$ of $G$.
